padaccheda: अथ । अवनिपयःतेजःपवनानाम् । युगक्षये । जाते । परमसंक्षोभे । बभूव । अस्मिन् । जगत्त्रयम्
anvaya: अथ युगक्षये अवनिप-तेजः-पवनानाम् परम-संक्षोभे जाते (सति) अस्मिन् जगत्त्रयम् (तादृशम्) बभूव।
meaning_english: Then, at the end of the age, when a supreme agitation of the earth, fire, and wind occurred, the three worlds became thus transformed.
The universe shone with clouds of ash resembling a forest of dark Tāpiccha trees in flight; it was a whirling mass of smoke, moving like the Great Ocean's massive whirlpools.
Resounding with the playful 'timi-timi' roar of dancing blue flame-fragments, the inner spaces of the worlds were filled with a dense mass of ashen clouds.
With long, leaping cries of 'chama-chama' acting as trumpets, the universe echoed with the spreading victory-shout of the rising downpour.

The three worlds were filled with wandering ash-clouds and smoky mists, characterized by the confusion of great dissolution-clouds, like fierce masses of clouds wandering in the delusion of vaporous mists.
Through the blasts of wind, terrifying with their 'bhāṅkāra' echoes against the walls of the universe, heaps of burnt cities of Indra and other gods were tossed into the sky.
The sense of hearing was deafened by the 'ṭaṅkāra' clanging produced by the collision of millions of stones bursting forth from the play of water, fire, and wind.
The universe resounded with the thick 'chama-chama' sound of the quenching of cosmic fires by dense rains, falling in continuous streams like pillars of the sky.

content_sanskrit: गङ्गा तरङ्गिका येषां तादृशैः सरितां गणैः । अभ्रैरिव नभोभीमैः पूर्यमाणाखिलार्णवम्
padaccheda: गङ्गा । तरङ्गिका । येषाम् । तादृशैः । सरिताम् । गणैः । अभ्रैः । इव । नभोभीमैः । पूर्यमाणाखिलार्णवम्
anvaya: (तत् जगत्त्रयम्) येषाम् गङ्गा तरङ्गिका (अस्ति) तादृशैः नभः-भीमैः अभ्रैः इव सरिताम् गणैः पूर्यमाण-अखिल-अर्णवम् (बभूव)।
meaning_english: All the oceans were being filled by hosts of rivers to whom the Gaṅgā was but a tiny ripple—rivers that appeared like clouds terrifying as the vault of heaven.
The orb of dissolution-clouds had its surface licked by the scorching suns, which appeared like clusters of flowers situated amidst a multitude of dark Tāpiccha leaves.
The universe was filled with flowing mountain-rivers, peaks, islands, and cities, while the intense agitation caused by the winds of cosmic dissolution pounded the mountains to pieces.

padaccheda: ग्रहतारागणैः । उग्रैः । व्यग्रैः । विग्रहदुर्ग्रहैः । पतद्भिः । द्विगुणालातलतामावर्तपातिभिः
anvaya: उग्रैः विग्रह-दुर्ग्रहैः व्यग्रैः पतद्भिः द्विगुण-आलात-लता-आवर्त-पातिभिः ग्रह-तारा-गणैः (व्याप्तम् आसीत्)।
meaning_english: The sky was filled with fierce, restless groups of planets and stars, difficult to perceive due to their clashing forms, falling like double-stranded whirling vines of firebrand-flames.
The world was shattered by the impact and bursting of massive mountains of water rising from the Āvaha wind, its floor strewn with the edges of mountains overturned by the great dissolution.
The atmosphere became sluggish and dense with darkness as the rays of the sun were blinded by solidified vapor-clouds and thick, fat clouds of the cosmic end.
The ocean became crowded and treacherous with fragments of the shattered earth-crust, crumbling coastlines, and the falling of rolling mountains being swept away.
The boundaries of the quarters were shattered by the deep, thunder-like roar of the ocean and by devouring winds that tore through clouds with stones uplifted by the waves.
The howling single ocean resounded with the sharp 'ṭāṃ' sounds of the cosmic egg's walls being struck, and the clapping impacts of the branch-like clouds of the Kalpa.

padaccheda: स्वर्गपातालभूर्लोकखण्डखण्डैः । विमिश्रितैः । यथास्वभावम् । तिष्ठद्भिः । मरुबुध्नैः । वृताम्बरम्
anvaya: विमिश्रितैः स्वर्ग-पाताल-भू-लोक-खण्ड-खण्डैः यथा-स्वभावम् तिष्ठद्भिः मरु-बुध्नैः वृत-अम्बरम् (आसीत्)।
meaning_english: The firmament was covered with intermingled fragments of heaven, the netherworld, and the earth-plane, along with the foundations of deserts remaining in their natural state.
The weapons of gods and demons were whirled about as they tossed in the winds, their bodies dead, half-dead, burnt, or half-burnt, yet appearing to confront one another.
Massive pillars known as white-whirlwinds were formed by the ashes and the dry grass of other worlds, all driven wildly by the winds of the Kalpa's end.
The sky resounded with the harsh, intense clanging of a calamitous era, as riverbanks crumbled under the impact of sweeping masses of rocks and entire worlds fell headlong.
The atmosphere blazed with the roaring echoes emanating from the caves of mountain ranges tossed by the winds, while the falling cities of the world-protectors created massive whirlpools in space.

padaccheda: कृतकर्कशनिर्ह्रादैः । असुरैः । इव । मारुतैः । उह्यमानवनव्यूहप्रोतवातायनैः । वृतम्
anvaya: कृत-कर्कश-निर्ह्रादैः असुरैः इव मारुतैः उह्यमान-वन-व्यूह-प्रोत-वातायनैः वृतम् (तत् व्योम)।
meaning_english: The sky was filled with fierce winds that shrieked like demons, carrying away entire forests which, tangled together, resembled windows through which the gale whistled.

padaccheda: पुरमण्डलदैत्याग्निसुरनागविवस्वताम् । निकुरम्बम् । दधत् । व्योम्नि । मशकानाम् । इव । उच्चयम्
anvaya: व्योम्नि मशकानाम् उच्चयम् इव पुर-मण्डल-दैत्य-अग्नि-सुर-नाग-विवस्वताम् निकुरम्बम् दधत् (तत् व्योम)।
meaning_english: The vast expanse of the sky held the multitudes of cities, demons, fires, gods, nāgas, and suns, all appearing as insignificant as a swarm of gnats.

padaccheda: नश्यन्नगवराभोगैः । भागैः । भग्नसुरालयैः । आवर्तघर्घरारावैः । जलम् । ऊर्ध्वम् । अधः । अनलम्
anvaya: नश्यत्-नग-वर-आभोगैः भग्न-सुर-आलयैः भागैः आवर्त-घर्घर-आरावैः ऊर्ध्वम् जलम् अधः अनलम् (तत्) कुर्वत्।
meaning_english: With the destruction of great mountain ranges and the shattering of divine abodes, the cosmic dissolution turned the waters above and the fires below into a chaotic mass of gurgling whirlpools.
The collision of waters and mountains pulverized the cities of the directional guardians, as the habitations of gods, daityas, siddhas, and gandharvas came crashing down.

content_sanskrit: कुट्टनं पर्वतादीनां प्रशान्ताङ्गाररूपिणाम् । वातैः कुर्वत्पदार्थानामसारं रजसामिव
padaccheda: कुट्टनम् । पर्वतादीनाम् । प्रशान्ताङ्गाररूपिणाम् । वातैः । कुर्वत् । पदार्थानाम् । असारम् । रजसाम् । इव
anvaya: प्रशान्त-अङ्गार-रूपिणाम् पर्वत-आदीनाम कुट्टनम् वातैः रजसाम् इव पदार्थानाम् असारम् कुर्वत्।
meaning_english: The winds pulverized mountains and other objects, which looked like extinguished embers, reducing substantial matter into a worthless heap of dust.

content_sanskrit: पुराण्यमरदैत्यानां भ्रमद्भित्तीनि शातयत् । रत्नैः खणखणायन्ति पयांसीव पयस्वताम्
padaccheda: पुराणि । अमरदैत्यानाम् । भ्रमद्भित्तीनि । शातयत् । रत्नैः । खणखणायन्ति । पयांसि । इव । पयस्वताम्
anvaya: भ्रमत्-भित्तीनि अमर-दैत्यानाम् पुराणि शातयत् पयस्वताम् पयांसि इव रत्नैः खणखणायन्ति।
meaning_english: As the spinning walls of the cities belonging to gods and demons were shattered, their scattered gems produced a clinking sound, like the splashing of water in great oceans.

padaccheda: पूर्णाम्बरम् । पतल्लोकलोकसप्तकमन्दिरैः । चक्रावृत्त्या । भ्रमद्रूपैः । अमरैः । सागरैः । इव
anvaya: पतत्-लोक-लोक-सप्तक-मन्दिरैः चक्र-आवृत्त्या भ्रमत्-रूपैः अमरैः सागरैः इव पूर्ण-अम्बरम् (अभवत्)।
meaning_english: The entire sky was filled with the falling temples of the seven worlds, while gods and oceans spun in circular motions like a revolving wheel.

content_sanskrit: डीनोड्डीनैः परिवृतं विचलद्वातवेल्लितैः । दग्धादग्धैः पदार्थैः खे शीर्णपर्णगणैरिव
padaccheda: डीनोड्डीनैः । परिवृतम् । विचलद्वातवेल्लितैः । दग्धादग्धैः । पदार्थैः । खे । शीर्णपर्णगणैः । इव
anvaya: विचलत्-वात-वेल्लितैः डीन-उड्डीनैः दग्ध-अदग्धैः पदार्थैः खे शीर्ण-पर्ण-गणैः इव परिवृतम्।
meaning_english: Tossed by the fluctuating winds, objects both burnt and unburnt flew through the air, covering the sky like a multitude of withered, fallen leaves.

anvaya: (तत् जगत्) उद्यत्-झण-झण-स्वनैः दिवः पतद्भिः हेम-स्फटिक-वैदूर्य-सुसार-मणि-मन्दिरैः आकीर्णम् (अभवत्)
meaning_english: The world was filled with the ringing sounds of gold, crystal, and lapis lazuli mansions falling from the heavens, scattering precious gems everywhere.

padaccheda: उत्पेतुः । धूमभस्माब्दाः । पेतुः । वाराः । पुरोत्कराः । उन्ममज्जुः । तरङ्गौघाः । ममज्जुः । भूतलाद्रयः
anvaya: धूम-भस्म-अब्दाः उत्पेतुः (च) पुर-उत्कराः वाराः पेतुः (च) तरङ्ग-ओघाः उन्ममज्जुः (च) भूतल-अद्रयः ममज्जुः
meaning_english: Clouds of smoke and ash rose up while masses of cities fell like water; waves of the ocean surged high as the mountains of the earth submerged.

padaccheda: आवर्तघर्घरारावाः । मिथः । विदलनोद्यताः । जुघूर्णुः । अर्णवाकीर्णपर्णवत् । प्रौढपर्वताः
anvaya: आवर्त-घर्घर-आरावाः मिथो विदलन-उद्यताः प्रौढ-पर्वताः अर्णव-आकीर्ण-पर्ण-वत् जुघूर्णुः
meaning_english: Massive mountains, making gurgling sounds in the whirlpools and ready to shatter one another, whirled around like fallen leaves scattered upon the ocean.

padaccheda: क्रन्दच्छिष्टामरगणम् । चलत्सज्जीवभूतकम् । भ्रमत्केतुशतोत्पातम् । दुष्प्रेक्ष्यम् । अभवत् । जगत्
anvaya: क्रन्दत्-शिष्ट-अमर-गणम् चलत्-सज्जीव-भूतकम् भ्रमत्-केतु-शत-उत्पातम् जगत् दुष्प्रेक्ष्यम् अभवत्
meaning_english: The universe became unbearable to behold, filled with the cries of surviving gods, the trembling of living beings, and the chaotic movement of hundreds of ominous comets.

padaccheda: मृतार्धमृतया । भूतसंतत्या । अनिललोलया । अभूत् । नीरन्ध्रम् । आकाशम् । जीर्णपर्णसवर्णया
anvaya: जीर्ण-पर्ण-सवर्णया अनिल-लोलया मृत-अर्ध-मृतया भूत-संतत्या आकाशम् नीरन्ध्रम् अभूत्
meaning_english: The sky became densely packed with a mass of dead and half-dead beings, tossed by the wind like withered leaves and sharing their pale color.
The world was filled with torrential rains as thick as falling mountain peaks and hundreds of rivers overflowing with moving mountains, cities, and gale-force winds.
The world contained fires making hundreds of crackling sounds as they were extinguished, and mountain slopes shimmering as they were tossed by the surging movements of the restless oceans.
The universe appeared fierce as islands and oceans mixed like straw in a stream, while the momentary flames reached toward the vast, distant sky of pure Consciousness (Cid-vyoma).
The world became a ghost of its former self, with celestial beings falling amidst the fragrance of ash from fires quenched by rain, its previous creation now entirely forgotten.
The world resounded with unrestrained noise, following the process of cosmic dissolution; though only the remnants of destruction remained, it was yet devoid of a final end to the cycle of creation.

padaccheda: अनारतविपर्यासकारिमारुतनिर्वृतम् । बीजराशिः । इव । अजस्रम् । पूर्यमाणम् । पुनः । पुनः
anvaya: अनारत-विपर्यास-कारि-मारुत-निर्वृतम् (यथा स्यात् तथा) अजस्रम् पुनः पुनः पूर्यमाणम् बीज-राशिः इव (तत् ब्रह्माण्डम् अभवत्) ।
meaning_english: The universe became like a heap of seeds, incessantly filled again and again as it was scattered by the winds that cause constant displacement and upheaval during the dissolution.
The hollow of the sky, resembling a golden floor, became filled with spreading dust particles born from the golden sparks and fire-powder produced by the mutual clashing of firebrands.
The seventh netherworld was completely filled with the falling massive fragments of the earth's surface, including islands and oceans, along with the rolling spheres of the subterranean regions.
From the depths of the seventh Sutāla realm to the mountains on the earth's surface and up to the sky, everything turned into a single vast ocean, filled with the destructive winds of pralaya.

content_sanskrit: एकार्णवोऽथ ववृधे शनै शीघ्रं सरिच्छतैः । भुवने जलकल्लोलैः कोपो मूर्खाशये यथा
padaccheda: एकार्णवः । अथ । ववृधे । शनैः । शीघ्रम् । सरिच्छतैः । भुवने । जलकल्लोलैः । कोपः । मूर्खाशये । यथा
anvaya: अथ भुवेन जल-कल्लोलैः एक-अर्णवः शनैः (तथा) शीघ्रम् सरित्-शतैः (तथा) ववृधे यथा मूर्ख-आशये कोपः (वर्धते) ।
meaning_english: Then, with hundreds of rivers and surging waves, the single cosmic ocean grew both slowly and rapidly across the world, just as anger intensifies within the heart of a fool.

padaccheda: मुसलोपमया । पूर्वम् । ततः । स्तम्भनिभाङ्गया । ततः । तालद्रुमाकारधारयासारसारया
anvaya: पूर्वम् मुसल-उपमया ततः स्तम्भ-निभ-अङ्गया ततः ताल-द्रुम-आकार-धारा-आसार-सारया (वृष्ट्या भुवने जलम् ववृधे) ।
meaning_english: The waters increased first through rain resembling clubs, then like massive pillars, and finally through the intense force of showers shaped like palm trees.
The deluge continued with water falling in singular, fierce torrents like river currents, delivered by clouds as thick and expansive as the surface of the earth's seven islands.

content_sanskrit: वह्निर्विदाहकृदृष्ट्या शममभ्याययौ तथा । शास्त्रसज्जनसंगत्या गाढमापत्पदं यथा
padaccheda: वह्निः । विदाहकृत् । दृष्ट्या । शमम् । अभ्याययौ । तथा । शास्त्रसज्जनसंगत्या । गाढम् । आपत्पदम् । यथा
anvaya: विदाह-कृत् वह्निः दृष्ट्या तथा शमम् अभ्याययौ यथा शास्त्र-सज्जन-संगत्या गाढम् आपत्-पदम् (शमम् याति) ।
meaning_english: The burning fire was extinguished by the downpour, just as a state of deep calamity is pacified through the study of sacred śāstras and the company of virtuous people.

padaccheda: ऊर्ध्वाधरस्थपरिवृत्तपदार्थजातम् । अन्तःकणैः । खणखणायितशैलमज्जम् । ब्रह्माण्डकोटरम् । अभूत् । विधुरम् । कुबाललीलाविलोलम् । इव । बिल्वफलम् । विशुद्धम्
anvaya: ऊर्ध्व-अधर-स्थ-परिवृत्त-पदार्थ-जातम् अन्तः-कणैः खण-खणायित-शैल-मज्जम् ब्रह्माण्ड-कोटरम् कु-बाल-लीला-विलोलम् विशुद्धम् बिल्व-फलम् इव विधुरम् अभूत् ।
meaning_english: With its contents tossed upside down and its mountain-cores clattering like internal seeds, the hollow of the universe became distressed, resembling a hollowed bilva fruit shaken playfully by a small child.
